questions.question: Who is the speaker of the speech 'A Great Son of India'?
questions.explanation: The speech was delivered by Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan, a great teacher and philosopher.

questions.question: On which occasion was this speech delivered?

options.B: The 92nd birth day of Swami Vivekananda
options.C: The opening of a new school

questions.explanation: Dr. Radhakrishnan speaks about the saint on his 92nd birth day.

questions.question: Swami Vivekananda is known for carrying the teachings of which ancient texts to the world?
questions.explanation: He carried the teachings of the Upanisads to the people of the world.

questions.question: Vivekananda was one of the great leaders of the ________.
questions.explanation: The speaker identifies him as one of the great leaders of the Indian Renaissance.

questions.question: What did Vivekananda interpret for the world?

options.C: The history of the British Empire

questions.explanation: He interpreted for us and the world India's religious consciousness, which are the treasures of her past.

questions.question: Who was Swami Vivekananda's 'great Master'?
questions.explanation: His writings and speeches were fortified by the sayings of his great Master, Shri Ramakrishna.

questions.question: What are the two dominant features of the modern age according to the speech?
questions.explanation: The two dominant features of our age are science and democracy.

questions.question: According to the speaker, educated people cannot accept faith without ________.
questions.explanation: Educated people cannot be asked to accept deliverances of faith without rational evidence.

questions.question: Religions practised today often seem unscientific and ________.
questions.explanation: The 'eclipse of religion' occurs because they seem both unscientific and undemocratic.

questions.question: What is described as the 'most obvious fact of life'?
questions.explanation: The speaker states that the most obvious fact of life is its transience, meaning everything passes away.

questions.question: What symbolizes time in India's tradition?
questions.explanation: Time is symbolized in India's tradition by birth and death.

questions.question: Great civilizations are subject to the law of ________.
questions.explanation: The text notes that great civilizations are subject to the law of time.

questions.question: The feelings of dread and anxiety bear witness to what?
questions.explanation: These feelings and the precariousness of the world bear witness to the world beyond.

questions.question: According to the great thinkers, the world is an expression of ________.
questions.explanation: Thinkers concluded there is a Beyond of which all this world is the expression.

questions.question: What are the Vedas, according to the registers mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: The Vedas are described as the registers of the spiritual experiences of the great seers.

questions.question: Vivekananda said the Vedas mean the 'accumulated treasure of ________ discovered by different persons'.
questions.explanation: He defined them as the accumulated treasure of spiritual laws.

questions.question: For Vivekananda, religion is defined as ________.
questions.explanation: For Vivekananda religion is Yoga, which means personal change and integration.

questions.question: Vivekananda wrote books on Jnana Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, Karma Yoga and ________.
questions.explanation: The text lists Jnana, Raja, Bhakti, and Karma Yoga as his subjects.

questions.question: What is 'religious conceit' according to the speaker?
questions.explanation: Intolerance is an expression of religious conceit and not humility.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say we are 'secular'?

options.B: We regard all religions as sacred.

questions.explanation: We are secular because we regard all religions as sacred and believe in freedom of conscience.

questions.question: Secularism requires us to do what regarding other religions?
questions.explanation: Secularism requires us not merely to tolerate, but to understand and love other religions.

questions.question: Vivekananda felt miserable about which issue in India?
questions.explanation: He felt miserable about India's backwardness and how religion was confused with obscurantism and superstition.

questions.question: Vivekananda protested vehemently against the abuse of religion regarding ________.
questions.explanation: He protested against our insistence on touchability and untouchability.

questions.question: What is 'antar-jyoti'?
questions.explanation: Antar-jyoti is the light which lighteth every man that cometh into the world, reflecting the Divine within.

questions.question: What are the ultimate tests of true religions?

options.B: Recognition of truth and reconciliation with human beings

questions.explanation: The ultimate tests are recognition of truth and reconciliation with human beings.

questions.question: Vivekananda raises work to the level of ________.
questions.explanation: He raises work to the level of worship.

questions.question: We should seek salvation through the ________.
questions.explanation: Vivekananda exhorted us to seek salvation through the service of God in man.

questions.question: Establishing a spiritual religion can bring society nearer to ________.
questions.explanation: Establishing such a religion brings society nearer to Ramrajya or the Kingdom of God.

questions.question: The term 'Renaissance' means ________.
questions.explanation: Glossary: renaissance - rebirth/reawakening of art, culture etc..

questions.question: What does the word 'transience' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: transience - lasting for a short time.

questions.question: What is 'ahimsa' according to the text?
questions.explanation: To overcome enemies we must possess ahimsa, or renunciation of hatred.

questions.question: The speaker distributed prizes for which competitions?
questions.explanation: Dr. Radhakrishnan mentions distributing prizes for recitation and speech competitions.

questions.question: Vivekananda prepared us for the new age of ________.
questions.explanation: His life and teachings prepared us for the new age of freedom.

questions.question: Any religion which supports ________ cannot commend itself to us today.
questions.explanation: A religion which divides man or supports privileges, exploitation, or wars cannot commend itself.

questions.question: Everything in this world ________, including the painted picture and carved stone.
questions.explanation: The text lists things that pass away, such as the written word, painted picture, and carved stone.

questions.question: What is the consequence of the sun aging and altering?

options.B: The earth may become unfit for human habitation.

questions.explanation: The earth may one day become unfit for human habitation as the sun ages and alters.

questions.question: Our acts, thoughts, and deeds of heroism are part of ________.
questions.explanation: They are part of history, of becoming, or process.

questions.question: Which ancient texts provide logical arguments and experiences of men bearing witness to the Supreme?
questions.explanation: The Upanisads mention logical arguments and experiences of men bearing witness to the reality of the Supreme.

questions.question: Vivekananda said, 'By the Vedas no ________ are meant.'
questions.explanation: He stated that by the Vedas no books are meant.

questions.question: Yoga involves reconditioning of one's ________.
questions.explanation: Religion as Yoga is the reconditioning of one’s nature.

questions.question: According to the speaker, what is 'religious conceit'?
questions.explanation: Intolerance is an expression of religious conceit.

questions.question: Vivekananda suggested praying in mosques and kneeling to the ________.
questions.explanation: He said Hindus unite with every religion, including praying in mosques and kneeling to the Cross.

questions.question: What term means 'the practice of opposing enlightenment'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: obscurantism - the practice of opposing enlightenment.

questions.question: What is described as 'operative and alive' within us?
questions.explanation: The great principle of our religion is that the Divine is in us, operative and alive.

questions.question: The 'light which lighteth every man' refers to ________.
questions.explanation: This light is called antar-jyoti and cannot be put out.

questions.question: What is the end goal of man, according to the text?
questions.explanation: The end of man consists in attaining union with the Divine.

questions.question: What is 'ahimsa' defined as in the context of overcoming enemies?
questions.explanation: Ahimsa is the renunciation of hatred which surpasses enmity.

questions.question: Spiritual religion should transcend ________ organizations.
questions.explanation: Spiritual religion transcends ecclesiastical organizations.

questions.question: What does 'vehemently' mean in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: vehemently - strongly / forcefully.

questions.question: Whose experience influenced Vivekananda's views on secularism?
questions.explanation: Bearing in mind Shri Ramakrishna’s experience, Vivekananda spoke about uniting with every religion.
